 Order

The complainant-petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the order dated 03.09.2016 passed by the learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ballari, in Criminal Revision Petition No.42/2016.

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties to this revision petition are referred to as per their ranking before the trial Court.

3. The facts leading up to this revision petition are as under:
The complainant filed a private complaint before the II Additional Civil Judge, JMFC Court, Ballari in P.C.No.157/2010, alleging that the accused has committed the offence punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 It is alleged in the complaint that, there exists a property bearing Door No.5,
old Door No.2, Ward No.23, situate in TS No.955/1, Tezab compound, Cowl Bazaar, Ballari,
measuring 226 X 22 feet.

entities.text: II Additional Civil Judge, JMFC Court, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said property was initially owned by one Raheem Bee wife of late Hussain Peeran.
The said Raheem Bee was none other than the complainant's father's sister.
There was a dispute with regard to the said property which went up to the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
With regard to the rival claims, a Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.10738/2003 was filed and the said SLP (Civil) was allowed and the matter was remanded to this Court in RSA No.206/1999.
The said Raheem Bee who was one of the opponents in the said case died during the year 2009, so also her husband predeceased her.
The said Raheem Bee had no issues, either male or female.
It was alleged that, the said property was gifted by her mother to her under the Mohammadan law by way of a settlement.
Her brother's father and mother were alive and they were the legal heirs of Raheem Bee.
It is stated in the complaint that, the accused is neither the legal heir NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 nor related to Raheembe.
But he is claiming as adopted son of Raheembe.
He is styling himself as the son of late Raheem Bee and created a document to that effect.

The Mohammadan law do not Mohammmed Khaleel vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147888293/
2 recognize the postiriarity and adoption.

sentences.text: Thus, the accused had no such right to claim his right in the said property.

It is alleged that, with dishonest intention and fraudulently to cheat the real legal heirs from claiming the same and creating false document thereby, the accused has not only cheated but also forged the document and made an attempt to use the said document as genuine.
Thereby he has committed the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468 and 471 of IPC.
Since the police did not take any action, the complainant filed a private complaint before the Court.
It is the further case of the complainant that, after the filing of the said complaint, it was referred to the police for investigation.
After investigation, the police filed B-final report.
Therefore, the complainant filed the protest petition before the JMFC Court.

The learned JMFC Court, NC:
2024:KHC-D:5238 after recording the sworn statement of the complainant, set aside the B-final report and took cognizance of the offence as per the orders dated 16.10.2015

. 
This order of taking cognizance and issuing process was challenged by the accused before the Principal Sessions Judge, Ballari, in Criminal Revision Petition No.42/2016.

The said Revisional Court on hearing the arguments of both the sides, and on perusal of the records, allowed the revision petition and set aside the order passed in P.C.No.157/2010 dated 16.10.2015 by the II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ballari.

entities.text: II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the said order, the complainant-petitioner is before this Court.
4. The respondent No.2 is served and remained unrepresented.

5. It is argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that, the allegations made in the complaint do demonstrate that the accused though no way connected to NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 the family of the Raheem Bee, but he is styling himself as adopted son of the said Raheem Bee.
She died issueless and even her husband died long back prior to her death.
It is the complainant and others, who are the legal heirs of the Raheem Bee.
Raheem Bee is none-else than the father's sister of the complainant i.e. she is the paternal aunt of the complainant.
Except the complainant and his other close relatives, there are no other legal heirs.
But even then, the accused is claiming his right, title and interest in the schedule property.
It is further submitted that, as there was a rival claim in respect of the said property there was a civil suit.
The said civil dispute went up to the Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP (Civil) No.10738/2003.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, remanded the matter to the High Court for deciding the matter afresh, which is pending in RSA No.206/1999 before this Court.

It is alleged that, because of concocting the documents and fabrication of the said documents,
the complainant was constrained to file the complaint.
It is submitted that, though the police filed B-report initially, NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 but the said B-report was challenged by the complainant by filing a protest petition.
Based upon the protest petition, the Magistrate rejected the B-final report and took cognizance.

According to his submissions, the learned JMFC Court, Ballari has rightly took cognizance of the offence, but the said order was challenged by the accused before the Sessions Court, but the Sessions Court has wrongly set aside the said order.

He submits that, as the said order is not properly reasoned and as the accused has created and fabricated the documents claiming to be the son of late Raheem Bee, therefore, the order passed by the Principal Sessions Judge, is required to be set aside and the orders passed by the II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ballari, is to be restored.

In support of his submissions, he relied upon the reasons being Mohammmed Khaleel vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147888293/
3 assigned by the Principal Sessions Judge, Ballari, in the course of the order.

sentences.text: 6. As against this submissions of the learned Addl.

SPP submits that, as a comprehensive civil suit is pending NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 in RSA No.206/1999 and the rival claims between the parties are yet to be decided, continuing this revision petition is nothing but a futile attempt by the complainant- revision petitioner.

He submits that, as already in the revision petition, the learned revisional Court has observed in the course of the order that, a civil suit is pending between the parties and the rights of the parties can be resolved there, there is no merit in this petition and it is further submitted by the learned Addl. SPP that, the claim of the petitioner is quite prematured.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsels from both sides.

8. In view of the rival submissions of both the sides, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the impugned order passed by the Principal Sessions Judge, Ballari, dated 03.09.2016 suffers from illegality and perversity and requires interference of this Court?"
NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 9.
On perusal of the allegations made in the complaint, it is the specific case of the complainant that,
he is the permanent resident of the Ballari district, Ballari
. There were house properties purchased by his father and uncle.
There was a dispute between his mother-in-law i.e. sister of the complainant's father by name Raheembe.
The said dispute went up to the Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP (Civil) No.10738/2003.
According to the complainant RSA No.206/1999 is still pending before the High Court of Karnataka.
According to him, Raheembe died in the year 2009 and her husband died long back prior to her death.
But the accused is claiming to be the son of the said Raheembe and claiming rights in the property of the said Raheembe.
He is claiming to be the adopted son, but such an adoption is not permissible under the Mohammadan law.

On the demise of the Raheembe,
the property will revert back to the legal heirs of the Raheembe.
The complainant is the brother's son of Raheem Bee, himself is the legal heir of the Raheem Bee.

It is alleged that, as there was a fabrication and correction of the documents by - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 the accused , the complainant filed a complaint and it was referred to the police for investigation.
The police filed B- final report.
The said B-final report was challenged by the complainant by filing protest petition.
Based upon that, after recording the sworn statement, the learned II Additional Civil Judge, Ballari, took cognizance of the offence punishable under Sections 420, 463, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
Accordingly, issued process against the accused.
But the learned Principal Sessions Judge by his order dated 03.09.2016 set aside the said order.

Evidently, in this case, it is an admitted fact that the rights of the parties in the present revision petition are ceased Mohammmed Khaleel vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147888293/
4 since RSA No.208/1999 is pending before this Court.

sentences.text:
As per the allegations made in the complaint,
the accused is claiming to be the adopted son of Raheem Bee.
But it is the case of the complainant that, the said Raheem Bee and her husband died issueless.
Raheem Bee died in the year 2009 and much prior to that, her husband died.
According to the complainant, the accused has created the documents.

During the course of order, the learned Sessions Judge has observed at page No.8 of the order,
stating that, "Civil dispute is pending between both the parties before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and that can be resolved there.
This complaint is nothing but abuse of process of law."
While observing so, the orders passed by the JMFC Court was set aside by the Principal Sessions Judge, Ballari.

It is admitted fact between both the sides that, the civil dispute is pending in RSA No.206/1999 before the High Court of Karnataka, the rights of the parties can very well be decided in the said civil suit.
It is submitted that, the said RSA came to be disposed of and the matter was remanded to the trial Court for fresh disposal.
If at all the allegations made in the complaint are true, the complainant can very well get redressal of his grievance by producing necessary documents and by leading oral evidence.

Even if the trial Court where the civil suit is pending, comes to the conclusion that, some illegal acts have been committed it can very well initiate the legal action against the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:5238 respondent under the relevant provisions of law.
As rightly observed by the revisional Court, the complainant can very well get his grievance redressed, since the dispute is of the civil nature.
Therefore, a liberty is very much available to get his grievance redressed.

Hence,
there is no merit in this revision petition.
Accordingly, the aforesaid point is answered against the petitioner.
Consequently, the petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed.
